risks.solution: Leaves turn bronze and dusty. Spray neem oil or an approved miticide at first bronzing and avoid dusty conditions.

risks.name: Blister Blight
risks.solution: Translucent blisters turn white on young leaves. Spray copper oxychloride weekly in the monsoon and pluck shoots regularly.

tips.title: Plant clonal cuttings 1.2 x 0.75 m apart
tips.description: Use certified clonal planting material and plant in pits.

tips.title: Grow shade trees
tips.description: Silver oak or Albizia give shade and protect from heat.

tips.title: Pluck two leaves and a bud
tips.description: Fine plucking gives the best quality leaf.

tips.title: Keep the soil acidic
tips.description: Avoid lime and use acidifying fertilizers.

risks.name: Tobacco Caterpillar

risks.name: Mosaic Virus
risks.solution: Leaves show light and dark green mottling. Use resistant varieties, control aphids and pull out sick plants.

risks.name: Damping Off
risks.solution: Seedlings collapse at the soil line in the nursery. Use raised beds and treated seed, and avoid over-watering.

tips.title: Raise healthy seedlings in a nursery
tips.description: Sow on raised beds and transplant at 6 to 8 weeks.

tips.title: Keep 90 x 60 cm spacing

tips.title: Top the plants at button stage

tips.title: Cure leaves as per grade
tips.description: Proper curing gives a better auction price and leaf colour.

weather.title: Rainfall Forecast
weather.description: Tomato seeds sprout best with 10 to 25 mm of rain in a week.

weather.title: Relative Humidity
weather.description: Tomato seeds sprout best when air humidity is 60% to 75%.

risks.name: Leaf Curl Virus
risks.solution: Leaves curl up and plants stay small. Raise the nursery under net, trap whitefly with yellow cards and pull out sick plants early.

risks.name: Early Blight
risks.solution: Brown rings appear on older leaves. Rotate with non-tomato crops and spray mancozeb as per label at the first spots.

risks.name: Fruit Borer
risks.solution: Caterpillars bore holes in the fruits. Set pheromone traps, grow marigold border rows and spray neem seed extract early.

risks.name: Bacterial Wilt
risks.solution: Plants wilt suddenly while the leaves stay green. Avoid fields with past wilt, use grafted or resistant seedlings and improve drainage.

tips.title: Transplant 25 day old seedlings
tips.description: Harden seedlings by cutting water for 2 days before moving to the field.

tips.title: Space plants 60 x 45 cm
tips.description: Wider spacing improves air flow and reduces blight spread.

tips.title: Stake plants within 3 weeks
tips.description: Staking keeps fruit off the soil and raises marketable yield.

tips.title: Use drip with mulch if possible
tips.description: Even moisture prevents fruit cracking and blossom end rot.

risks.name: Leaf Spot
risks.solution: Brown spots spread on leaves. Avoid overhead watering and crowding, and spray mancozeb as per label every 15 days.

risks.name: Flower Bud Borer
risks.solution: Buds have holes and drop. Collect and destroy damaged buds and spray neem seed extract at bud stage.

risks.name: Root Knot Nematode
risks.solution: Roots grow knots and plants stay stunted. Rotate with cereals, add neem cake before planting and avoid known infested fields.

tips.title: Plant bulbs of 2 to 3 cm
tips.description: Plant 5 cm deep at 30 x 30 cm. Use disease-free bulbs.

tips.title: Water every 7 days in dry months
tips.description: Keep soil moist during spiking and avoid waterlogging.

tips.title: Cut spikes when the lower buds open
tips.description: Cut spikes early in the morning for cut flower sale.

tips.title: Ratoon for 2 or 3 years
tips.description: Divide clumps after the first year for more bulbs.

risks.name: Rhizome Rot
risks.solution: Leaves yellow and the clump collapses with soft rhizomes. Use healthy seed rhizomes treated with mancozeb and plant on raised beds.

risks.name: Leaf Blotch
risks.solution: Brown blotches spread on leaves and they dry. Use healthy seed, avoid crowding and spray mancozeb as per label at the first spots.

risks.name: Shoot Borer
risks.solution: Central shoots dry (dead hearts) with holes in the stem. Cut and destroy affected shoots and spray neem seed extract from July.

tips.title: Treat seed rhizomes before planting
tips.description: Dip in mancozeb and Trichoderma to prevent rot.

tips.title: Plant on raised beds, 45 x 25 cm
tips.description: Beds drain well and protect rhizomes from rot.

tips.title: Mulch twice with green leaves
tips.description: Mulch at planting and at 50 days to cut weeds and hold moisture.

tips.title: Harvest when the leaves dry up
tips.description: Boil and dry the rhizomes within 3 days for good colour.

risks.name: Fruit Fly
risks.solution: Young fruits rot and drop with maggots inside. Put up cue-lure traps and collect fallen fruits.

risks.name: Powdery Mildew
risks.solution: White powder covers leaves. Avoid a dense canopy and spray wettable sulphur or hexaconazole as per label.

risks.name: Fusarium Wilt
risks.solution: Vines wilt suddenly and the stem base turns brown. Use resistant varieties, rotate with cereals for 4 years and treat seed with Trichoderma.

tips.title: Sow on raised beds with mulch
tips.description: Mulch warms the soil, saves water and keeps fruit clean.

tips.title: Keep 2.5 x 0.6 m spacing
tips.description: Sow 3 seeds per hill and thin to one.

tips.title: Cut water at fruit ripening
tips.description: Less water raises sweetness and avoids cracking.

tips.title: Check ripeness by tendril and sound
tips.description: A dry tendril and a dull thump show ripe fruit.

risks.name: Yellow Rust
risks.solution: Yellow stripes run along the leaves. Grow resistant varieties and spray propiconazole as per label at the first stripes.

risks.name: Aphid
risks.solution: Small green insects gather on ear heads in cold weather. Spray neem seed extract early and use imidacloprid only if they cover the ears.

risks.name: Termite
risks.solution: Plants dry up in patches with mud tubes at the base. Mix well rotted manure and treat seed before sowing in light soils.

tips.title: Sow 40 kg seed per acre in rows
tips.description: Keep 20 cm between rows. A seed drill gives an even stand and easy weeding.

tips.title: Treat seed before sowing
tips.description: A fungicide seed treatment protects against smut and seed diseases from day one.

tips.title: Give the first water at 21 days
tips.description: Irrigate at crown root stage. This decides how many tillers form.

tips.title: Finish sowing by mid December
tips.description: Yield drops with every day of delay, so sow on time.
